By assuming that all of the side faces have the same height $(8\,\text{in}),$ find the total surface area of the square pyramid above by considering its net.
question.worked_solution:
The net of our pyramid is as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249141/assets/c4a5fe995aaaf47b7ab2b90492059d739fc2352955dc1e12a71852fc13046a33.png)

First, notice that the base of the pyramid is a square with sides equal to $5 \, \text{in}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\text{Area of square} = 5 \times 5 = 25 \, \text{in}^2.
$$

 

Each side face of our solid is triangle, where the base is $5\,\text{in}$ and the height is $8\,\text{in}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\text{Area of triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 8 = 20 \, \text{in}^2.
$$

Finally, the surface area of the pyramid consists of $1$ square (the base) and $4$ triangles (the side faces). 

Adding the areas, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =1\times (\text{Area of the square})+4\times (\text{Area of the triangle}) \\  & =1\times 25+4\times 20 \\  & =25+80 \\  & =105\,{\text{in}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
